scope: Rigid whole-blade cant up to the 15-degree E1 study ceiling on the PROTOTYPE 3:1 / 24 m / X 25 m blades. Geometry only: no emissivity, temperature, Heat Debt, dose, activation or structural load. configuration.EVA.radiator_cant_deg stays known = false.

hinge_modes.aft_in: In-plane rotation about the tangential axis through the root station (X -6.0 m, r 24.0 m); the 98.1 m aft span moves toward the ship axis.
hinge_modes.fore_in: Same axis, opposite sense; the 31.0 m forward span moves toward the hull.
hinge_modes.edge: Out-of-plane rotation about the blade root edge (parallel to X at r 24.0 m); all three blades turn the same way.

method.sky_escape: 96 cosine-weighted rays from 24 points per face; blockers are the other blades (zero-thickness plates), the 6.5 m body envelope over the ship length and six COAST pod shield cylinders at one rotor phase. Truss members are not modelled, so absolute values run above the Blender screen; use the change with angle.
method.radiation: Line of sight from 37 fusion-core envelope samples through the PROTOTYPE shadow-shield slab; blades counted as baffles only in the shield_and_blades rows. Face flux proxy is the mean |cos incidence| / distance^2 from unobstructed core samples, relative to 0 deg.
method.clearance: Blade truss envelope (±1.64 m out of plane, +0.3 m at the edges) against the 6.5 m body, the rotor sweep (both rotor planes, pod shield outer radius) and the other blades; required 0.5 m. Plume clearance is not screened because the drive is OFF in EVA.

observations: Reactor view of the EVA access is set by the shadow shield alone: the airlock hatch sees 0% of core samples and the hull route from the radiator roots to the cage end 10% on average (21% of route points see some of the core, all at X -12.0 to -6.3 m against the shield's aft face at -11.5 m). Blades change these by at most 0.000 in any mode up to 15 deg, because those sight lines stay far inside the 24 m blade root radius.

In-plane cant keeps each blade in its radial plane, which contains the ship axis, so blade baffling of work sites 1.5 m off the faces barely moves (core share blocked by blades 0.22 at 0 deg, 0.26 aft_in and 0.21 fore_in at 15 deg). The edge hinge turns one face of each blade away from the core: 0.39 blocked and 25% of work sites fully shadowed at 15 deg, while direct core flux on the blade faces rises x3.01.
Clearance-limited angle within the 15 deg ceiling: aft_in 13.2 deg (aft blade ends meet behind the ship), fore_in 7.1 deg (forward outer corner enters the rotor sweep), edge 15.0 deg.

Sky escape against 0.952 at 0 deg: aft_in -0.023, fore_in +0.007, edge +0.001 at 15 deg. Only aft_in lowers it steadily (blades converge aft and see each other more); fore_in opens the aft span slightly, and edge stays within -0.004 to +0.002 over all angles, inside the ray-sampling scatter.
Blade share inside the shield's point-source shadow: 3.1% at 0 deg; at 15 deg aft_in 0.6%, fore_in 6.9%, edge 3.1%. Direct core flux on the faces: aft_in x1.34, fore_in x0.81.

In-plane cant about the root station moves the root-boom ends by up to 1.55 m and the aft-stay end by 7.15 m at 15 deg, so booms or stays must telescope. The edge hinge leaves all three attachment lengths unchanged because they sit on the hinge line.
owner_questions: Which hinge does "whole-petal root cant" mean for the longitudinal blades: in-plane about a tangential axis (which end moves inward?) or about the root edge?
What should the EVA cant protect: EVA crew at the hull and airlock (already set by the shadow shield), crew working on the blades, or scatter toward the pods?
